{{short description|Irish mathematician (born 1982)}}
{{use Hiberno-English|date=May 2013}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2017}}
'''Sarah Flannery''' (born 1982, [[County Cork]], Ireland) is an Irish mathematician who was, at sixteen years old, the winner of the 1999 [[Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition|Esat Young Scientist Exhibition]] for her development of the [[Cayley–Purser algorithm]], based on work she had done with researchers at [[Baltimore Technologies]] during a brief internship there.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.zdnet.com/home-and-office/networking/rsa-weighs-in-on-teens-breakthrough/|title=RSA weighs in on teen's 'breakthrough'|last=Staff|first=ZDNet|work=ZDNet|date=20 Jan 1999|access-date=23 September 2017}}</ref> The project, entitled "Cryptography – A new algorithm versus the [[RSA (algorithm)|RSA]]", also won her the [[European Union Contest for Young Scientists|EU Young Scientist of the Year Award]] in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|date=12 October 1999|title=Winners of the EU Young Scientists Competition|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/article/id/13762-winners-of-the-eu-young-scientists-competition|access-date=19 February 2021|website=cordis}}</ref>

==Biography==
Flannery's education included a primary all-girls school and secondary education at Scoil Mhuire Gan Smál in Blarney.<ref name=pm/>

Following the competition win, in 2001 Flannery co-authored ''In Code'' with her father,<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Gribbin |first=Ben |title=Review of 'I Got Algorithm', by Sarah Flannery, David Flannery |magazine=Books Ireland |number=236 |year=2000 |pages=360–62 |doi=10.2307/20632220|jstor=20632220 }}</ref> mathematician David Flannery (1952-2023).<ref>[https://www.echolive.ie/corknews/arid-41200963.html Cork mathematician David Flannery, father of songwriter Mick, dies aged 71] [[The Echo (Cork)|The Echo]], 08 AUG, 2023</ref> It tells the story of the making and breaking of the Cayley-Purser algorithm, as well as the enjoyment she got from solving mathematical puzzles while growing up. She dedicates many of her accomplishments in the fields of mathematics and cryptography to her father's support during her childhood.

She studied [[computer science]] at [[Peterhouse]], a college of the [[University of Cambridge]], graduating in 2003, and, as of 2006, worked for [[Electronic Arts]] as a software engineer. She worked at [[TirNua]] as a "Chief Scientist".<ref>[http://sims.stratics.com/ TirNua's Team Have EA in Common] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130528002950/http://sims.stratics.com/ |date=28 May 2013 }}</ref> She developed the virtual economy in a game and the back-end web services that powered the game features. She has also worked at RockYou, and several other institutions involved in software development and computer science.<ref name=pm>{{Cite web|url=http://planetmath.org/sarahflannery|title=Sarah Flannery|author=Miravinci|date=22 March 2013|website=planetmath.org|accessdate=23 September 2017}}</ref>

Before working at TirNua, Flannery was software engineer working directly with then Electronic Arts Worldwide Chief Technology Officer, Scott Cronce, and, later, with many fellow TirNua founders on her first virtual world.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://venturebeat.com/2013/07/28/eas-top-geek-scott-cronce-steers-us-through-gamings-future-technology-interview/ | title=EA's top geek Scott Cronce steers us through gaming's future technology (Interview) | date=28 July 2013 }}</ref>

At EA, she successfully set up the EA Open Source program using the Essential Project. Flannery created data visualizations on software architecture and game content creation which were used to directly impact the quality of both. She also successfully ran and turned around the virtual economy within EA-Land (formerly [[The Sims Online]]).

Previously, she worked on the technical and scientific computing software product [[Wolfram Mathematica|Mathematica]] for [[Wolfram Research]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://company.wolfram.com/announcements/2000/mathematica-and-the-science-of-secrecy/|title=Wolfram Research Announcements » Mathematica and the Science of Secrecy|website=company.wolfram.com|access-date=23 September 2017}}</ref>

The lights on St. Patrick's Street, one of the main thoroughfares of Flannery's home city of Cork, are named after her.

Flannery is the sister of the singer and songwriter [[Mick Flannery]].<ref name="My Holidays">{{cite news|author=Genevieve Carbery|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/travel/2009/0418/1224244965886.html|title=My Holidays|date=18 April 2009|access-date=9 January 2010|newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]|quote=I visited my sister [the former Young Scientist winner Sarah Flannery] in San Francisco.}}</ref>
